body: 18-key Almenraeder/Heckel bassoon, no serial (made before Heckel numbered), Murry Collection, Tennessee (database id Heckel1-O-Murry); bocal: the original bocal of the Grenser 13-key bassoon, Historisches Museum Basel (database id GrenserH3-O-Basel1904.312)
body c. 1840-1850 (sheet); bocal c. 1764-1813 (the maker's dates on the sheet)
body: Almenraeder/Heckel system, 18 keys, not the modern Heckel system; the pitch input of the authors' program is 440 Hz, a best guess, not a measurement
body: Murry Collection, Tennessee; bocal: Historisches Museum Basel; neither accessible to FrankenSim
assembled; unfolded into one series, bocal to bell, the boot's two bores joined at the septum

NOT the instrument of the UIowa bassoon recordings (a modern instrument whose system the Iowa pages do not give); an openly measured historical bassoon used as a labelled stand-in, with a bocal from another instrument and a modern plastic reed from another source
Heckel1-O-Murry measured 17 Sept of the year the sheet prints as 20124 (General Information sheet), data sheet PDF last modified 2024-10-23
GrenserH3-O-Basel1904.312 measured 25 Jan 2011 (its General Information sheet); original bocal 'yes' (data sheet row 1)

hole numbers 01 to 23 counted from the reed end by the axial position of the hole centre; the table geometry-report.txt maps each number to the sheet's name, bore and key; the wing's high A and high C vent holes and the long joint's B and Bb touches are NOT on the sheets and are omitted
every number was parsed from the pdftotext -layout text of the sheets by build-tables.py (row number and label asserted) and re-parsed independently by check-tables.py; nothing was typed by hand
